newsitem.title: UKRAINE: U.S. delays ban on Air Ukraine's Il-62s to April.
newsitem.headline: U.S. delays ban on Air Ukraine's Il-62s to April.

text.p: State-owned Air Ukraine said on Monday U.S. air authorities had agreed to wait until April next year before implementing anti-noise legislation against its Soviet-built Ilyushin-62s.
Valentyn Tyshchenko, a top aide to Air Ukraine's president, said the ban had been due to come into force on January 1 but would be delayed to give them time to lease quieter craft.

A final decision on whether to lease Boeing-767s or A-310 and A-320 Airbuses for Air Ukraine's existing routes to New York, Chicago and Toronto, and from April to Miami and Los Angeles, would be taken in early December, he added.

"We have got an agreement that the ban will come into effect in April next year, and not right from the new year," Tyshchenko said by telephone. "Il-62s will fly to North America until we lease the new Western-made planes."
Air Ukraine said in July it would lease two Boeing-767s but in September Vice-President Oleh Narizhny said the carrier would lease A-310s and A-320s instead.
Tyshchenko denied reports in Ukrainian media that the airline had dropped plans to lease Airbuses because of pressure from U.S. authorities to take Boeings instead.
"There is no pressure. Like any customer we take the best option based on price and reliability," Tyshchenko said.
"What is certain is that whatever plane we choose, Il-62s will fly to the United States until April."
The leasing is to be concluded via a joint venture set up with U.S. firm Crusader Holding WW Ltd with a capital of $250 million.
Air Ukraine operates more than 200 Soviet-made planes, including Tupolev 153 and 134, Antonov 24, and Yakovlev 40 and 42 aircraft. It also operates one leased Boeing 737.
